method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: QUOTED from International Braz J Urol 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review' (published online 20 December 2025), 19 claims; LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC13124169). S2: QUOTED from Bonomi M, Balsamo A, Bizzarri C, Gianfrilli D, et al., SIAMS and SIEDP, Journal of Endocrinological Investigation 49(7):1443 (doi 10.1007/s40618-026-02849-9) 'Management of andrological disorders from childhood and adolescence to transition age: guidelines from the Italian Society of Andrology and Sexual Medicine (SIAMS) in collaboration with the Italian Society for Pediatric Endocrinology and Diabetology (SIEDP) - part-2' (published 28 February 2026), 14 claims; LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC13451516). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the SIAMS/SIEDP 2026 society guideline (GRADE-rated recommendations; micropenis chapter), which fills the page's testosterone-dose gap. All S1 claims are unchanged. Both sources are CC BY 4.0 and quoted. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S1 Table 2 (penile-length nomograms) and Table 3 (hormone regimens in published studies), and S2 Table 3 (features suggesting a DSD) and Table 6 (conditions associated with micropenis). S2 Tables 2, 4, 5 and 7–9 have merged cells or ragged rows and were not extracted.

claims.claim: **Micropenis is a structurally normal penis with a stretched penile length (SPL) 2.5 SD or more below the mean** for age and stage of sexual development.
claims.source_text: Micropenis is a clinical diagnosis characterized by a structurally normal, albeit small, penis … The condition is defined by a Stretched Penile Length (SPL) that falls 2.5 standard deviations (SD) or more below the mean in a chart for a patient's age and level of sexual development
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Treat it as a sign, not just a finding:** in infancy or childhood it often points to a significant congenital or acquired endocrine disorder.
claims.source_text: The identification of micropenis in infancy or childhood is of paramount importance, as it is frequently the presenting sign of a significant underlying congenital or acquired endocrinopathy
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (CHH) is the commonest known cause.** Syndromes include Prader-Willi, Kallmann and Klinefelter.
claims.source_text: The most common underlying known cause is Congenital Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism (CHH), a failure of the testosterone axis (). Furthermore, micropenis can be a feature of numerous genetic syndromes, such as Prader-Willi, Kallmann, and Klinefelter syndrome, making its recognition a key step in a broader diagnostic workup
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A full medical evaluation is essential**, because associated conditions can be life-threatening, e.g. hypoglycaemia from panhypopituitarism.
claims.source_text: A full medical evaluation is essential not only to address the penile size itself but also to diagnose and manage potentially life-threatening associated conditions, such as hypoglycemia in cases of panhypopituitarism
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **It usually reflects too little androgen during a critical window:** from 12 weeks' gestation through the postnatal 'mini-puberty' of the first six months.
claims.source_text: The condition is most often a consequence of insufficient androgen stimulation for penile growth during a critical window of fetal development, specifically from 12 weeks of gestation through the postnatal "mini-puberty" in the first six months of life.
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Refer every infant with congenital micropenis for complete clinical and endocrine evaluation by a specialised multidisciplinary team** to exclude hormonal or syndromic causes (SIAMS/SIEDP R3.1: 1, ⊕⊕⊕⊕).
claims.source_text: R3.1 We recommend that infants with congenital micropenis need to be considered for a complete clinical and endocrine evaluation by a specialized multidisciplinary team to exclude all hormonal or syndromic causes of the condition (1, ⊕⊕⊕⊕).
claims.locator: Bonomi M, Balsamo A, Bizzarri C, Gianfrilli D, et al., SIAMS and SIEDP, Journal of Endocrinological Investigation 49(7):1443 (doi 10.1007/s40618-026-02849-9), 'Management of andrological disorders from childhood and adolescence to transition age: guidelines from the Italian Society of Andrology and Sexual Medicine (SIAMS) in collaboration with the Italian Society for Pediatric Endocrinology and Diabetology (SIEDP) - part-2', published 28 February 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13451516/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Time the hormone tests: in the first 2 days of life or in the minipuberty window (3 to 6 months),** measure testosterone, LH, FSH, inhibin B and AMH (R3.2: 1, ⊕⊕⊕○). This is the only window in which the physiological rise can be seen.
claims.source_text: R3.2 We recommend that newborns with isolated micropenis, regardless of subsequent diagnostic investigations, carry out a hormonal work-up during the first 2 days of life or during the minipuberty window (3 to 6 months of life), assessing the basal pituitary-gonadal function (Testosterone, LH, FSH, Inhibin B and AMH serum levels) (1, ⊕⊕⊕○). … A sample collected during the first 2 days of life or during the minipuberty window (3 to 6 months of life), as above mentioned, is the unique temporal opportunity to highlight any physiological rise in gonadotropins and testosterone to evaluate the functioning of the pituitary-gonadal axis
claims.locator: Bonomi M, Balsamo A, Bizzarri C, Gianfrilli D, et al., SIAMS and SIEDP, Journal of Endocrinological Investigation 49(7):1443 (doi 10.1007/s40618-026-02849-9), 'Management of andrological disorders from childhood and adolescence to transition age: guidelines from the Italian Society of Andrology and Sexual Medicine (SIAMS) in collaboration with the Italian Society for Pediatric Endocrinology and Diabetology (SIEDP) - part-2', published 28 February 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13451516/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Newborn features that suggest a disorder of sex development (S2 table) include micropenis,** along with overt atypical genitalia, apparent male genitalia with both testes undescended, isolated perineal hypospadias, mild hypospadias with an undescended testis, a family history of DSD, and genitalia that do not match a prenatal karyotype.
claims.source_text: [Table 3] Age-specific clinical features suggestive of Disorders of Sex Development (DSD) [Table 3 row 1] Newborn: 1. Overt atypical genitalia … [Table 3 row 3] Newborn: 3. Apparent male genitalia with bilateral undescended testes … [Table 3 row 4] Newborn: 4. Micropenis … [Table 3 row 5] Newborn: 5. Isolated perineal hypospadias … [Table 3 row 6] Newborn: 6. Mild hypospadias with undescended testis … [Table 3 row 7] Newborn: 7. A family history of DSD … [Table 3 row 8] Newborn: 8. A discordance between genital appearance and a prenatal karyotype

claims.claim: **Conditions associated with micropenis (S2 table).** Hypogonadotropic: isolated, combined with other pituitary deficiencies, or syndromic (Prader-Willi, Bardet-Biedl, Laurence-Moon, CHARGE, Silver-Russell, Rud), and isolated GH or IGF-1 deficiency. Gonadal (hypergonadotropic): anorchia; disorders of gonadal development (sex chromosome mosaicism, partial gonadal dysgenesis); androgen synthesis defects (3β- and 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, 17,20-lyase and 5α-reductase deficiency); partial androgen insensitivity; chromosomal or genetic syndromes (Klinefelter and multiple-X, Down, Noonan, Robinow, CHARGE); and penile agenesis. Miscellaneous: maternal antifungal use, environmental endocrine disruptors, and nonspecific 46,XY DSD or idiopathic micropenis.

claims.claim: **Diagnosis is clinical and depends on accurate SPL measurement.** Use a standard technique (SPLINT): supine, foreskin retracted if possible, rigid ruler pressed into the suprapubic fat, penis stretched to resistance, and at least two (preferably three) readings.
claims.source_text: The diagnosis of micropenis is clinical, based on an accurate measurement of SPL. … Note the private ambient room, supine position, foreskin retraction (for those who doesn't have phimosis), use of rigid ruler with zero-error correction and the compression over the suprapubic fat. The penis is stretched vertically to the point of resistance without causing discomfort. At least two (preferably three) measurements are obtained to ensure reproducibility.
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Penile size varies by ethnicity and region, so use the most relevant, current, population-specific nomogram**; local reference data are best.
claims.source_text: there is a significant finding in the literature about the well-documented variation in penile size across different ethnic and geographic populations. This has led to the development of numerous population-specific nomograms. … clinicians should use the most relevant, up-to-date, and population-specific data available to accurately diagnose micropenis and local data record charts are undoubtedly the best way to diagnosis micropenis
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Practical cut-offs (S2, citing international guidelines): under 2 cm at birth and under 4 cm after 5 years of age.** Record girth at the base and coronal level, palpate the corpora and check for cryptorchidism (R3.3: 1, ⊕⊕⊕⊕).
claims.source_text: According to international guidelines, micropenis is generally defined as < 2 cm at birth and < 4 cm after 5 years of age … Penile girth should be recorded at both the base and coronal level … R3.3 We recommend that children/adolescents with isolated idiopathic micropenis have an accurate measurement of the stretched penile length, palpation of the corporeal bodies with measurement of girth/diameter, and evaluation for cryptorchidism (1, ⊕⊕⊕⊕).
claims.locator: Bonomi M, Balsamo A, Bizzarri C, Gianfrilli D, et al., SIAMS and SIEDP, Journal of Endocrinological Investigation 49(7):1443 (doi 10.1007/s40618-026-02849-9), 'Management of andrological disorders from childhood and adolescence to transition age: guidelines from the Italian Society of Andrology and Sexual Medicine (SIAMS) in collaboration with the Italian Society for Pediatric Endocrinology and Diabetology (SIEDP) - part-2', published 28 February 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13451516/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Measured in the first 12 hours of life, stretched length may read about 10% short: measure again.** For karyotype, count more metaphases (e.g. 100) to find hidden mosaicism; FISH for SRY can exclude a DSD faster.
claims.source_text: When SPL is measured in the newborn during the first 12 h of life the length may be reduced by approximately 10% and should be reassessed … A standard karyotype does not allow to highlight possible hidden mosaicisms thus a higher number of metaphases (e.g., n = 100) is always needed to improve accuracy []; karyotype may be preceded whenever possible by a fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) for the sex-determining region on the Y chromosome (SRY) for a faster exclusion of a DSD condition
claims.locator: Bonomi M, Balsamo A, Bizzarri C, Gianfrilli D, et al., SIAMS and SIEDP, Journal of Endocrinological Investigation 49(7):1443 (doi 10.1007/s40618-026-02849-9), 'Management of andrological disorders from childhood and adolescence to transition age: guidelines from the Italian Society of Andrology and Sexual Medicine (SIAMS) in collaboration with the Italian Society for Pediatric Endocrinology and Diabetology (SIEDP) - part-2', published 28 February 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13451516/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Population nomograms reviewed by S1:** Indian (2014; 200 boys aged 0–10 y), Japanese (2015; 1628, 0–7 y), Turkish (2021; 948 uncircumcised boys), Egyptian (2023; 1500 prepubertal boys), Brazilian preterm newborns (2025; 140, measured within 72 h and weekly), Brazilian (2007; 2,010, 0–18 y, by age and Tanner stage), Chinese (2018; 2,974 urban boys, 0–17 y) and Bulgarian (2010; 6,200 white boys, 0–19 y).

claims.claim: **First steps: counselling, investigation of the endocrine cause, and hormone therapy** aiming for a length within the normal range for age.
claims.source_text: The initial objectives of micropenis management are counseling, investigation of underlying endocrinological causes (as often as possible) and hormonal therapy, with the goal to stimulate penile growth to achieve a length that is within the normal range for age.
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hormone therapy is the most accepted and effective treatment, especially in CHH,** though some boys, particularly with severe hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, do not reach a normal adult size.
claims.source_text: The most widely accepted and effective treatment for micropenis, which can be particularly effective in cases of CHH, is hormonal therapy, but some patients may not reach normal adult penile size, especially in cases of severe hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give testosterone early: infancy or early childhood, including mini-puberty, gives the best growth.** Earlier start means more growth; initial glans width is a strong predictor of response.
claims.source_text: the optimal timing for testosterone therapy to achieve the best response in penile growth for patients with micropenis is during infancy or early childhood, including the period of mini puberty. Early initiation of therapy is associated with greater penile growth, and initial penile dimensions - particularly glans width - are strong predictors of response
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitor for premature virilisation and high serum testosterone, particularly with topical preparations.**
claims.source_text: Monitoring for side effects such as premature virilization and elevated serum testosterone is recommended, particularly with topical therapy.
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The evidence is thin:** there are no large, long-term placebo-controlled trials and no evidence-based guideline on testosterone for micropenis. Short-term results are favourable; long-term data are limited.
claims.source_text: There are no large, placebo controlled, long-term studies and evidence-based guidelines directly addressing testosterone therapy for micropenis … While short-term outcomes are favorable, long-term data are limited, and randomized placebo-controlled trials are lacking.
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Expectant management may suit selected boys**, since many untreated patients normalise at puberty. It must be individualised, with structured clinical and psychosocial follow-up; the supporting studies had high drop-out.
claims.source_text: Emerging evidence suggests that many untreated patients may achieve normalization of penile size during puberty, supporting expectant management in selected cases. However, methodological limitations - particularly high attrition rates - restrict the generalizability of this approach. Any expectant strategy must be individualized and accompanied by structured clinical and psychosocial follow-up.
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Surgery is not first line.** Keep it for failed hormone therapy or anatomical abnormality; paediatric outcomes are poorly documented and the risks significant.
claims.source_text: Surgical options are reserved for cases where hormonal therapy fails to achieve adequate penile length, or in the presence of anatomical abnormalities. … Surgical intervention, as documented in medical literature, is not a first-line treatment for micropenis in children. Surgical techniques are complex and include procedures like the release of the suspensory ligament () and neo phalloplasty. The outcomes of these surgeries in the pediatric population are not well-documented, and they carry significant risks, making hormonal therapy the preferred initial approach.
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Testosterone injection regimens in S1's study table (not recommendations):** testosterone enanthate 25 mg IM every 4 weeks up to 4 times (53 Japanese prepubertal boys; median gain 0.6 cm); 25 mg IM monthly for 3 months in boys under 11 (Nerli, more than 100% SPL increase); and 25–50 mg IM every 4 weeks for 3 months in 8 males with CHH, then adult dosing, with no significant difference between starting in infancy or childhood.
claims.source_text: [Table 3] Hormonal Management of Micropenis. [Table 3 row 1] Reference Number: Ishii et al. 2004 () · Study type, Substance(s), Patient Cohort: Prospective, Testosterone Enanthate (TE), 53 Japanese prepubertal boys. · Posology: 25mg IM every 4 weeks, up to 4 times. · Key Outcomes & Remarks: Effective: Median SPL increment of 0.6cm, independent of age or gene polymorphisms. … [Table 3 row 3] Reference Number: Bin-Abbas et al. 1999 () · Study type, Substance(s), Patient Cohort: Retrospective, Testosterone Enanthate (TE), 8 males (-y) with CHH. · Posology: 25-50mg IM every 4 weeks for 3 months (- courses), then dose increased to adult regimen. · Key Outcomes & Remarks: Long-Term Success: No significant difference between early (infancy) vs. late (childhood) treatment. … [Table 3 row 4] Reference Number: Nerli et al. 2013 () · Study type, Substance(s), Patient Cohort: Retrospective, TE vs. hCG, 25 boys with isolated non-syndromic micropenis. · Posology: TE (<11y): 25mg IM monthly for 3 months. hCG (>11y): 1,500-2,000 IU IM weekly for 6 weeks. · Key Outcomes & Remarks: Significant Growth: >100% increase in SPL in both groups. No adverse effects reported.

claims.claim: **hCG in S1's study table:** 1,500–2,000 IU IM weekly for 6 weeks in boys over 11 (Nerli, 25 boys, more than 100% SPL increase alongside the testosterone group); and in 20 patients with CHH, 1,500–2,000 IU IM three times a week for 8 weeks, with a mean SPL gain of 2.31 cm and good tolerance.

No adverse effects reported. … [Table 3 row 5] Reference Number: Becker et al. 2016 () · Study type, Substance(s), Patient Cohort: Retrospective, hCG, 20 patients with CHH. · Posology: 1,500-2,000 IU IM, 3x/week for 8 weeks. · Key Outcomes & Remarks: Effective for IHH: Mean SPL increased 2.31 cm. Safe and well-tolerated.

claims.claim: **Topical and DHT regimens in S1's study table:** 5% testosterone cream (10 mg) daily for 30 days raised SPL by about 44% in 50 boys aged 5 months to 8 years, with only mild transient local hyperpigmentation or eczema; 2.5% DHT gel at 0.1–0.2 mg/kg/day for up to 6 months brought 61% of 23 boys to a normal SPL (above −2.5 SD) without bone-age advance.
claims.source_text: [Table 3 row 6] Reference Number: Arisaka et al. 2001 () · Study type, Substance(s), Patient Cohort: Prospective, Topical Testosterone, 50 prepubertal boys (5mo-8y). · Posology: 5% cream (10mg) applied daily for 30 days. · Key Outcomes & Remarks: Significant Growth: Mean SPL increased ~44%,. Minimal Side Effects: Mild, transient local hyperpigmentation/eczema. No skeletal effects. … [Table 3 row 7] Reference Number: Xu et al. 2017 () · Study type, Substance(s), Patient Cohort: Open Prospective, DHT Gel, 23 boys (9mo-11y) with normal karyotype. · Posology: 2.5% gel (0.1-0.2 mg/kg/day) applied daily for up to 6 months. · Key Outcomes & Remarks: High Success Rate: 61% achieved normal SPL (> -2.5 SD). 26% clinically improved. Safe: No bone age acceleration or systemic side effects.
claims.locator: International Braz J Urol, 'Micropenis in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review', published online 20 December 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13124169/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **DHT versus testosterone enanthate (Karrou 2023, as tabulated by S1):** in 49 boys, DHT 5 mg daily for 5 weeks (renewed 1–2 times) against testosterone enanthate 50 mg IM monthly (renewed once) gave mean growth of +2.37 cm versus +1.82 cm (p = 0.008), with no side effects; the sample was small and there was no genetic testing.
claims.source_text: [Table 3 row 2] Reference Number: Karrou et al. 2023 () · Study type, Substance(s), Patient Cohort: Prospective, Transdermal Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) vs. TE, 49 boys without hypogonadism or genetic syndromes. · Posology: DHT: 5mg daily for 5 weeks (renewed 1-2 times). TE: 50mg IM monthly (renewed once). · Key Outcomes & Remarks: DHT Superiority: Mean growth DHT +2.37 cm vs. TE +1.82 cm (p=0.008). No Side Effects Critique: Small sample size, no genetic testing.

claims.claim: **Treat isolated idiopathic micropenis found early in life in a paediatric endocrinology centre** (R3.7: 1, ⊕⊕○○). With established androgen sensitivity, testosterone or DHT may be given in the first 6 months of life or later in childhood or adolescence (R3.8: 2, ⊕⊕○○).
claims.source_text: R3.7 We recommend that isolated idiopathic micropenis discovered early in life is treated by a pediatric endocrinology center (1, ⊕⊕○○). … R3.8 We suggest that patients with idiopathic micropenis and established androgen sensitivity, may be treated with testosterone/DHT therapy during the first 6 months of life or later in childhood/adolescence to stimulate the growth of the penis (2, ⊕⊕○○).

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suggested regimen: testosterone enanthate 25 mg IM once a month for 3 months in prepubertal children, repeatable only once after 3–6 months; or transdermal DHT 5 mg daily for 6 weeks, repeatable 1–2 times.** No evidence supports hormone therapy after puberty.
claims.source_text: Based on the available evidence we thus suggest using T enanthate 25 mg i.m. in prepubertal children once a month for 3 months, repeatable only once after 3-6 months; or transdermal DHT (5 mg/daily for 6 weeks, repeatable 1-2 times). No evidence supports the use of hormonal therapies after puberty.

claims.claim: **The evidence behind it:** there is no consensus on age, dose, route or duration. Testosterone enanthate 25 mg IM monthly for 3 months more than doubled penile length in prepubertal boys (durability unknown), with the same result reported in minipuberty; 5% testosterone cream (10 mg daily on the penis for 30 days) and low-dose local DHT (0.1–0.3 mg/kg/day for 6 months) also increased length.
claims.source_text: There is no consensus on the age, dosage, method of administration, or duration of T or DHT therapy in boys with isolated micropenis. A regimen of intramuscular depot-testosterone enanthate 25 mg administered monthly for 3 months has been reported to show an increase in penile length of over 100% in prepubertal boys with isolated micropenis. However, the study does not provide information on the long-term durability of the results achieved … The same results with Te enanthate at the same dosage are reported also during minipuberty … Arisaka et al. also documented a significant increase in SPL in 50 prepubertal boys treated with T cream 5% (10 mg/daily applied directly to the penis) for a duration of 30 days. … short term (6 months) and local application of DHT at low doses (0.1-0.3 mg/kg/day) in patients with micropenis could accelerate penile growth effectively without evident side effects

claims.claim: **In a randomised study of 49 children and adolescents (mean age 9.7 years), transdermal DHT (5 mg daily for 5 weeks) outperformed testosterone enanthate (50 mg IM monthly for 3 months):** mean gain 2.82 versus 1.87 cm, both significant.
claims.source_text: A recent randomized study on 49 patients compared the efficacy of transdermal DHT (5 mg/daily for 5 weeks with 1 or 2 repetitions if necessary) and T enanthate (50 mg i.m. monthly for 3 months, with 1 repetition if necessary) in treating isolated idiopathic micropenis in children and adolescents (mean age 9.7 ± 4.4years). The study suggested a superiority of transdermal DHT compared to injectable exogenous T in the treatment of idiopathic micropenis, although both showed significant penis enlargement (mean penile size increment 2.82 vs. 1.87 cm, respectively)

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Testosterone enanthate and DHT gel are off label in children (at least in Italy), so obtain signed informed consent from parents;** DHT is not available everywhere, and whether very early treatment improves adult length is still unclear.
claims.source_text: Moreover, T enanthate and DHT gel is off label for treatment during pediatric age (0-18 yrs.), at least in Italy, and an informed, signed consent need to be obtained by parents/legal representative of the minor. Furthermore, it should be considered that DHT is not available in all countries. … There is still uncertainty about the optimal age of therapy with androgens for maximal effect; given that tissue AR expression is high in early infancy, it would seem appropriate to use androgens at that point, but it remains unclear whether such early use of androgens has any benefit on penile length in adulthood

claims.claim: **Minipuberty:** if androgen deficiency is found then, low-dose testosterone may be considered; gonadotropin therapy to recreate minipuberty has more limited reports. Both are off label.
claims.source_text: In cases where androgen deficiency is detected during minipuberty, early treatment with low-dose T may be considered to support normal genital development [-]. There are also more limited reports suggesting the use of gonadotropin therapy to replicate the missed minipuberty [, ]. Nonetheless, it should be emphasized that both mentioned therapeutic approaches are currently considered off label.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Recommend against surgery before adulthood** (R3.9: 1, ⊕⊕○○). During transition, counsel with extreme caution about surgery because function is uncertain and complications are frequent.
claims.source_text: R3.9 We recommend against surgical therapy before adulthood, postponing this option in adult life (1, ⊕⊕○○). … During the transition process the adolescents/young adults must be counseled by expert personnel and advised with extreme caution about surgical options due to uncertain functional efficacy and the high rate of complications among patients with micropenis

claims.claim: **Follow-up:** review at least once before puberty and regularly from expected puberty (R3.4: 1, ⊕⊕⊕⊕); offer psychosocial support to the family and the boy (R3.6: 2, ⊕⊕○○).
claims.source_text: R3.4 We recommend reviewing the patient with isolated idiopathic micropenis at least once in the prepubertal period and regularly from the time of expected puberty on to evaluate the development of sexual characteristics and possible supportive hormonal therapy (1, ⊕⊕⊕⊕). … R3.6 We suggest that the family and/or the patient with micropenis should already be offered competent psychosocial attendance by a professional familiar with problems of the genito-urinary tract (2, ⊕⊕○○).
